title: Get your agent ready for website design
description: Set up one practice folder, give a clear design brief and check a focused first page.
summary: A clear brief beats a vague design request. Build one page, then polish what matters.
cardSummary: One folder. One useful page. A brief you can copy.
installationMode: Manual project context in Claude Desktop; no third-party skill installation
sourceCaveats: English captions reviewed; no sampled frames or reproduction
Creator price, valuation and speed claims are unverified
Third-party skill installers and hosting offers excluded
body:
Website design / Source reviewed

Get your agent ready for website design.

Turn a rough idea into one focused page. Start with a clear brief, then improve the result in small passes.

You will make: a local one-page prototype with a useful headline, one main action and a mobile layout.

Before you start: a Windows or macOS computer, a browser, eligible Claude Code access and text/images you own. Account cost and usage limits depend on your plan.

  1. Open one practice folder

    Use the official Claude Desktop setup. Install the app for your computer, sign in with eligible access and open the Code tab. Choose a new local folder such as website-practice. Existing users can start here. Check current access and cost before subscribing.

  2. Give it direction

    Paste the brief below into your session. Replace the brackets. Attach your own logo or screenshots you have permission to use. Describe what you like about a reference; ask for an original design.

  3. Build the useful part first

    Ask for a static index.html using plain HTML and CSS, with no packages or external services. Review the proposed sections before building. Keep the first version to one page and one primary action.

  4. Check, then polish

    Open index.html in your browser. Narrow the window and tab through links. Check readable text, visible focus, working anchors and your main action. Ask for one repair pass with the actual problems you found. Add motion only when it clarifies feedback, with a reduced-motion option.

Stuck? If Code is unavailable, check account eligibility in the official setup guide. If the page fails, share the browser error and expected result. To undo, keep wanted files and delete the practice folder.

Copy this starter brief

Create an original one-page website for [audience] who need [outcome].
Main action: [one action]. Sections: introduction, benefits, example, FAQ, final action.
Style: [three concrete traits]. Use my supplied content; mark missing facts as TODO.
First propose two visual directions and ask only questions that block the build.
Then make index.html with plain HTML/CSS and minimal JavaScript. No packages,
tracking, network calls, accounts or deployment. Use system fonts and owned assets.
Make it readable on phones, keyboard usable and respectful of reduced motion.
Report what you checked and what I still need to check.
Source, requirements & limits

Adapted from Metics Media, Build $10,000 Websites using Claude Code (Ultimate Guide): brief and references at 06:02; review and polish at 15:54; mobile pass at 20:52. 1,308,220 views checked 14 November 2026; highest-viewed website tutorial in our five-result shortlist.

This is our original simplified workflow. It uses pasted project context. The source's global skill installs, external components and paid hosting are outside this guide. English captions were reviewed; sampled frames were unavailable after media retrieval stalled. Subscription cost and usage vary; no installation, generated website, usability benefit, commercial value or revenue was tested here. Official desktop instructions checked 14 November 2026.

title: Turn scattered sources into a marketing brief
description: Use a browser notebook to build a concise campaign brief with claims you can trace.
summary: Collect three good sources, ask focused questions and check the evidence before writing.
cardSummary: Three sources in. One campaign brief out. Every claim checked.
installationMode: Browser notebook; no packages or skill installation
requirements: Three public or owned source documents
sourceCaveats: English captions reviewed; no sampled frames or reproduction
2024 source interface and limits differ from current documentation
Current official help labels the product Gemini Notebook; source video calls it NotebookLM
No campaign performance or revenue measured
body:
Marketing / Source reviewed

Turn scattered sources into a marketing brief.

Make one useful campaign brief from material you already trust. Keep every factual claim connected to its source.

You will make: a short brief with an audience, one message, supporting evidence and unanswered questions.

Before you start: a browser, eligible Google account and three public or owned documents: a product fact sheet, an audience note and a past campaign recap. Use synthetic examples for practice. Keep customer details out.

  1. Open your notebook

    Open Google's notebook app and create a notebook named after your campaign. No local installation is needed. The tutorial calls it NotebookLM; current official help calls it Gemini Notebook. Check your account's availability and limits before starting.

  2. Add a small source set

    Choose Add sources and upload or paste your three documents. Give each a clear title and date. Open each imported source to confirm the important text arrived. Select only sources relevant to this campaign.

  3. Ask for the evidence first

    Paste the prompt below. Open each citation and compare it with the original document. Remove unsupported benefits and separate customer evidence from assumptions. A citation is a route to check, not a guarantee.

  4. Write and save your brief

    Ask for a 150-word brief using only verified findings. Include audience, message, proof, one call to action and open questions. Copy it into your own document and keep its source links. Review tone and facts yourself before sharing.

Copy this research prompt

Using only the selected sources, prepare evidence for a campaign about [offer].
List: audience needs, supported benefits, common objections and missing facts.
For every factual point, cite the supporting source. Label assumptions clearly.
If the sources disagree, show the disagreement. Do not invent customer quotes,
statistics, testimonials, pricing or results. Finish with three questions I must answer.

Check your result: every fact has supporting text; no invented quotes; dates are visible; unanswered questions remain open. If import fails, try an owned text document rather than a blocked page. To undo, delete the practice notebook and any exported copies you no longer need.

Source, cost and review coverage

Inspired by Jeff Su, Learn 80% of NotebookLM in Under 13 Minutes!, especially source selection/citation checks (00:36-06:00) and campaign project context (08:09-09:46). 1,838,492 views checked 14 November 2026; highest-viewed relevant tutorial in our five-result research shortlist.

We reviewed English captions, not continuous video or sampled frames. This original marketing exercise has not been reproduced. The source dates from December 2024; its product limits and interface are historical. We checked Google's source-import instructions and availability guidance on 14 November 2026. Account restrictions and paid allowances may vary. No paid plan is required by this guide; no campaign or revenue outcome was measured.
